text:
Avery: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — want to capture the main customer win/loss themes and clear next steps. TL;DR: wins = reliability + predictable costs; losses = integration friction and latency spikes in POCs. Asking leadership: which of the top asks should we prioritize for next quarter?

Samir: Thanks — can you paste the brief signal list? I'm particularly curious about the latency POC reports.

Avery: Sure. Copied from notes: 1) Customers chose us for stable tail latencies and predictable unit cost. 2) We lost deals where the SDK integraton took >2 weeks or required infra changes. 3) Several regulated customers want VPC/on-prem proofs but hit onboarding delays. 4) Two deals cited intermittent 500s during heavy burst tests.

Maria: Adding: a few customers explicitly asked for "per-route token visibility" in the console so security teams can audit usage. That came up twice in enterprise loses.

Talia: Re: integration friction — are we sure it's SDK docs or the auth/connector flow? I saw one note about opaque API errors during key rotation.

Avery: Good point. From the sales notes: one was docs, one was key rotation error (500 with no body), and one was needing a dedicated connector for a legacy broker.

Samir: For leadership asks: prioritize (A) quick SDK doc refresh + a 1-page integration checklist, (B) improving key-rotation error visibility (make 5xx include correlation_id and user-facing hint), (C) a 2-week "POC acceleration" concierge for top enterprise prospects. Which of these do we turn into a sprint?

Jeff: From product side I'd push (B) and (A) first — low lift, high signal. (C) is high touch and should be handled by customer success + solutions, but we can support with templates.

Maria: +1 on correlation_id for errors. We had a lost deal where customer ops couldn't debug within a day. Correlation ids would've saved it.

Talia: For the latency spikes: can eng-runtime share whether those were due to cold starts, batching config, or specific model variants? ops-bot: run latency-summary for 2025-10-01..2025-11-30?

ops-bot: @Talia requested latency summary. Query queued: job id 7783. ETA ~3m.

Avery: Also leadership question: customers asked for clearer pricing examples for mixed workloads (retrieval + generation). Is that a docs copy change or do we want a small pricing calculator?

Samir: I'd vote for a pricing calculator + sample scenarios. Sales needs something to show buyers quickly. Docs alone won't sell the value.

Jeff: We can ship a simple calculator widget in the console and a one-pager with 3 scenarios. Low dev effort if we reuse existing per-token model.

Maria: Actionable asks I'm putting in the tracker: 1) SDK doc refresh (owner: DevEx) 2) correlation_id + better 5xx (owner: Eng Runtime) 3) pricing calculator + scenarios (owner: Product) 4) POC concierge workflow draft (owner: CS + Solutions) 5) per-route token audit UI (owner: Console)

Talia: Small note — for (2) let's make sure errors during key rotation also return a clear HTTP status and a link to a KB note. That was a specific customer ask.

Avery: Can leadership confirm priority ordering? From today's vibe I'd rank: (2) errors + correlation_id, (1) SDK docs, (5) audit UI, (4) POC concierge pilot, (3) pricing calc. But I'm flexible.

Jeff: Leadership note: we will commit to (2) and (1) in Q1 cycle. (5) we'll scope as a discovery in Q1. (4) and (3) are Q2 work but we'll start templates for (4) now.

Samir: Thanks. I'll put together a 1-page exec summary for the next PM sync with owners/ETA.

Maria: One more customer insight — several customers said they liked that we routed fallback to smaller quantized variants automatically. That's a clear win we should highlight in sales collateral.

Avery: Great — Samir, can you include that as a win in the summary? Also capture the two loss cases with 500s and the SDK timeline.

Samir: Yep — will have draft by EOD tomorrow.

Talia: ops-bot job done: latency summary attached (link: https://internal/redwood/jobs/7783). Quick glance: most spikes aligned with bursty eval jobs hitting dedicated pools at 3-4x baseline.

Jeff: That suggests we need better admission control or burst protection on Dedicated pools — adding to eng-runtime backlog.

Maria: Who owns the "per-route token audit" ask? We need an initial mock to show security teams — even a simple CSV export would help.

Avery: Console team (Jeff) to own an export prototype. Can we aim for a CSV export in 3 weeks?

Jeff: Yes, CSV export prototype in 3 weeks. I'll assign to design + frontend.

Samir: Thanks everyone. I'll post the summary and the action tracker link here when ready. :thumbsup:

Avery: Thanks — this is helpful. If anyone has customer quotes that should be anonymized into the win/loss doc, drop them in the doc Samir will share. :raised_hands:
